title: Delhi PM2.5 Analysis (2022)
text: V5GL04 NetCDF files store data [lon, lat] order — reverse terra expects ([lat, lon]). Loading entire 121MB global array just extract Delhi extremely slow (~30 minutes 12 months). two helpers read pixels covering Delhi’s bounding box, making extraction near-instant.
code: # read_v5gl04_fast(): returns a single mean PM2.5 value for the shape # Used for the monthly time series (Section 1) read_v5gl04_fast <- function(nc_path, shape) {   bbox <- sf::st_bbox(shape)    nc   <- ncdf4::nc_open(nc_path)   lons <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "lon")   lats <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "lat")    # Find only the lon/lat indices that fall within Delhi's bounding box   lon_idx <- which(lons >= bbox["xmin"] & lons <= bbox["xmax"])   lat_idx <- which(lats >= bbox["ymin"] & lats <= bbox["ymax"])    # Read only that small subset (~50x50 pixels) instead of the full global array   delhi_data <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(     nc, "GWRPM25",     start = c(min(lon_idx), min(lat_idx)),     count = c(length(lon_idx), length(lat_idx))   )   ncdf4::nc_close(nc)    mean(delhi_data, na.rm = TRUE) }  # load_v5gl04_rast(): returns a terra SpatRaster cropped to Delhi # Used when we need the full spatial raster (Sections 2, 3, 4) load_v5gl04_rast <- function(year, month, shape) {   nc_path <- sprintf(     "/NAS/climatehealth/WUSTL_PM2.5/V5GL04/Global/Monthly/V5GL04.HybridPM25.Global.%04d%02d-%04d%02d.nc",     year, month, year, month   )   bbox <- sf::st_bbox(shape)    nc   <- ncdf4::nc_open(nc_path)   lons <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "lon")   lats <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "lat")    lon_idx <- which(lons >= bbox["xmin"] & lons <= bbox["xmax"])   lat_idx <- which(lats >= bbox["ymin"] & lats <= bbox["ymax"])    delhi_data <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(     nc, "GWRPM25",     start = c(min(lon_idx), min(lat_idx)),     count = c(length(lon_idx), length(lat_idx))   )   ncdf4::nc_close(nc)    # Build a raster from the Delhi subset   # V5GL04 stores [lon, lat] — transpose and flip vertically to get [lat, lon]   r <- terra::rast(     nrows = length(lat_idx), ncols = length(lon_idx),     xmin  = min(lons[lon_idx]), xmax = max(lons[lon_idx]),     ymin  = min(lats[lat_idx]), ymax = max(lats[lat_idx]),     crs   = "EPSG:4326"   )   terra::values(r) <- t(delhi_data)[nrow(t(delhi_data)):1, ]   r }

code: # Download per-station data for winter months: Oct, Nov, Dec, Jan # Winter is the policy-relevant season — highest PM2.5, highest health risk if (!dir.exists("station_data")) dir.create("station_data")  station_raw <- lapply(seq_along(delhi_station_list$value), function(i) {   id   <- delhi_station_list$value[i]   file <- paste0("station_data/", id, ".csv")    tryCatch({     # Cache per-station files — download only if not already saved     if (!file.exists(file)) {       cpcb_download_station_data(         station_id    = id,         year          = 2022,         save_location = file       )     }     df <- read.csv(file)      df %>%       pivot_longer(cols = -Day, names_to = "Month_Name", values_to = "pm25") %>%       mutate(month = match(Month_Name, month.name)) %>%       filter(month %in% c(1, 10, 11, 12), !is.na(pm25)) %>%       summarise(ground_pm25 = mean(pm25, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%       mutate(value = id)    }, error = function(e) {     # Skip stations that fail — CPCB data has occasional gaps     message("Skipped: ", id)     data.frame(value = id, ground_pm25 = NA)   }) })  station_ground <- do.call(rbind, station_raw)  # Join ground readings with station coordinates station_ground_sf <- station_ground %>%   filter(!is.na(ground_pm25)) %>%   left_join(delhi_station_list %>% select(value, lat, lon), by = "value") %>%   filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon)) %>%   sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)  cat(nrow(station_ground_sf), "stations with valid winter PM2.5\n") #> 39 stations with valid winter PM2.5

text: V5GL04 NetCDF files store data [lon, lat] order — reverse terra expects ([lat, lon]). Loading entire 121MB global array just extract Mumbai extremely slow. two helpers read pixels covering Mumbai’s bounding box, making extraction near-instant.
code: # read_v5gl04_fast(): returns a single mean PM2.5 value for the shape # Used for the monthly time series (Section 1) read_v5gl04_fast <- function(nc_path, shape) {   bbox <- sf::st_bbox(shape)    nc   <- ncdf4::nc_open(nc_path)   lons <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "lon")   lats <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "lat")    lon_idx <- which(lons >= bbox["xmin"] & lons <= bbox["xmax"])   lat_idx <- which(lats >= bbox["ymin"] & lats <= bbox["ymax"])    mumbai_data <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(     nc, "GWRPM25",     start = c(min(lon_idx), min(lat_idx)),     count = c(length(lon_idx), length(lat_idx))   )   ncdf4::nc_close(nc)    mean(mumbai_data, na.rm = TRUE) }  # load_v5gl04_rast(): returns a terra SpatRaster cropped to Mumbai # Used when we need the full spatial raster (Sections 2, 3, 4) load_v5gl04_rast <- function(year, month, shape) {   nc_path <- sprintf(     "/NAS/climatehealth/WUSTL_PM2.5/V5GL04/Global/Monthly/V5GL04.HybridPM25.Global.%04d%02d-%04d%02d.nc",     year, month, year, month   )   bbox <- sf::st_bbox(shape)    nc   <- ncdf4::nc_open(nc_path)   lons <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "lon")   lats <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "lat")    lon_idx <- which(lons >= bbox["xmin"] & lons <= bbox["xmax"])   lat_idx <- which(lats >= bbox["ymin"] & lats <= bbox["ymax"])    mumbai_data <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(     nc, "GWRPM25",     start = c(min(lon_idx), min(lat_idx)),     count = c(length(lon_idx), length(lat_idx))   )   ncdf4::nc_close(nc)    # Build a raster from the Mumbai subset   # V5GL04 stores [lon, lat] — transpose and flip vertically to get [lat, lon]   r <- terra::rast(     nrows = length(lat_idx), ncols = length(lon_idx),     xmin  = min(lons[lon_idx]), xmax = max(lons[lon_idx]),     ymin  = min(lats[lat_idx]), ymax = max(lats[lat_idx]),     crs   = "EPSG:4326"   )   terra::values(r) <- t(mumbai_data)[nrow(t(mumbai_data)):1, ]   r }

text: Mumbai 2022: Monthly PM2.5 satellite ground sources. sources agree seasonal pattern — peak winter, trough monsoon. text: Vayuayan (वायुअयन) combines two Sanskrit words: Vayu (वायु): Wind, air Ayan (अयन): Path, journey, movement Together, “Vayuayan” means “path wind” — representing journey movement air quality data across space time.

code: library(vayuayan)  # Get list of available states states <- cpcb_get_state_list() print(states)  # Get cities in a state cities <- cpcb_get_city_list("Maharashtra") print(cities)  # Get stations in a city stations <- cpcb_get_station_list("Mumbai") print(stations)  # Add coordinates from CPCB live feed stations <- cpcb_add_coords(stations) print(stations[, c("label", "lat", "lon")])  # Download city-level daily PM2.5 data cpcb_download_city_data(   city          = "Mumbai",   year          = 2022,   save_location = "mumbai_aqi_2022.csv" )  # Download per-station daily PM2.5 data cpcb_download_station_data(   station_id    = "site_5964",   year          = 2022,   save_location = "station_data_2022.csv" )

title: vayuayanR - Air Quality Data Analysis for India
code: library(vayuayan)  # Get mean PM2.5 statistics for a region from WUSTL ACAG NetCDF delhi_stats <- pm25_get_stats(   geojson_file = "delhi_ncr.geojson",   year         = 2022,   month        = 11 ) print(delhi_stats) # Returns: list(mean, std, min, max, count)  # Get PM2.5 statistics grouped by a column in the GeoJSON state_stats <- pm25_get_stats(   geojson_file = "india_districts.geojson",   year         = 2022,   month        = 11,   group_by     = "state_name" ) print(state_stats)  # Download a NetCDF file manually pm25_download_netcdf(   year      = 2022,   month     = 11,   cache_dir = "pm25_data" )

title: vayuayanR - Air Quality Data Analysis for India
code: library(vayuayan) library(tidyverse)  # Download and reshape city-level data cpcb_download_city_data("Delhi", 2022, "delhi_aqi_2022.csv")  delhi_monthly <- read.csv("delhi_aqi_2022.csv") %>%   pivot_longer(cols = -Day, names_to = "Month_Name", values_to = "pm25") %>%   mutate(month = match(Month_Name, month.name)) %>%   filter(!is.na(pm25)) %>%   group_by(month) %>%   summarise(mean_pm25 = mean(pm25, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")  # Plot seasonal trend ggplot(delhi_monthly, aes(x = month, y = mean_pm25)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1, color = "#d77027") +   geom_point(size = 2.5, color = "#d77027") +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +   labs(     title = "Delhi 2022: Monthly Mean PM2.5",     y     = expression(paste("PM2.5 (", mu, "g/m"^3, ")")),     x     = NULL   ) +   theme_minimal()

title: vayuayanR - Air Quality Data Analysis for India
code: library(vayuayan) library(sf) library(ggplot2)  # Get stations and add coordinates from CPCB live feed stations    <- cpcb_get_station_list("Delhi") stations_sf <- cpcb_add_coords(stations) %>%   filter(!is.na(lat)) %>%   sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)  # Plot ggplot(stations_sf) +   geom_sf(size = 3, color = "royalblue4", alpha = 0.8) +   labs(     title   = "CPCB Monitoring Stations — Delhi",     caption = "Source: CPCB CAAQMS"   ) +   theme_minimal()
